method: S1 is the open RACGP AJGP 2021 review, fetched and checked verbatim (34 claims, 4 of them doses that are machine re-checkable). A1 is AMH, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED across the 'Dry eye syndrome' and 'General principles: topical eye drugs' topics (34 claims, 6 doses); no passage reproduced, no source_text stored, each claim carries its page's locator. AMH's 'Comparison of ocular lubricants' table lists roughly 40 branded products with their preservatives; NO product row is reproduced, because reproducing a licensed product table is redistribution and because AMH itself states there is no evidence any lubricant is superior to another. What is carried instead is the PRESERVATIVE distinction, which both sources say is the choice that matters. S1's doxycycline dose for posterior blepharitis fills a hole the conjunctivitis-and-eye-infections guideline recorded as input_unavailable; that guideline was NOT edited, because its claim set was verified against its own sources and this dose comes from a different one.

claims.claim: Dry eye disease is a common disorder that negatively affects quality of life, is in most cases not curable and involves mainly symptomatic management even when ophthalmologist referral is indicated
claims.source_text: Dry eye disease (DED), also known as 'keratoconjunctivitis sicca', is a common disorder that negatively affects the quality of life of hundreds of millions of people around the world. 1,2 … DED, in most cases, is not curable and involves mainly symptomatic management, even when ophthalmologist referral is indicated.

claims.claim: The TFOS DEWS II definition describes dry eye as a multifactorial disease of the ocular surface characterised by loss of homeostasis of the tear film and accompanied by ocular symptoms, in which tear film instability and hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation and damage, and neurosensory abnormalities play aetiological roles
claims.source_text: Dry eye is a multifactorial disease of the ocular surface characterised by a loss of homeostasis of the tear film and accompanied by ocular symptoms in which tear film instability and hyperosmolarity, ocular surface inflammation and damage, and neurosensory abnormalities play etiological roles.

claims.claim: One study showed the prevalence of dry eye disease is approximately 7.4% in the Australian adult population, and the Blue Mountains Eye Study reported in 2003 showed 57.1% of the older population had one dry eye symptom
claims.source_text: One study showed the prevalence of DED is approximately 7.4% in Australia in the adult population, 7 and the Blue Mountains Eye Study (reported in 2003) showed that 57.1% of the older population had one DED symptom.

claims.claim: The tear film has a volume of approximately 7 to 10 microlitres and is composed of three layers from superficial to deep: lipid, aqueous and mucin
claims.source_text: The tear film has a volume of approximately 7-10 µL 10 … The tear film is composed of three layers, starting from superficial to deep: lipid, aqueous and mucin.

claims.claim: Dry eye disease is universally accepted as either evaporative dry eye or aqueous deficient dry eye, both resulting in increased tear film osmolarity, producing a hyperosmotic and desiccating environment that stimulates innate inflammatory events
claims.source_text: DED is now universally accepted as either evaporative dry eye (EDE) or aqueous deficient dry eye (ADDE). 1 ADDE is as a result of increased tear film osmolarity due to hyposecretion of the lacrimal gland. 9 EDE is also a result of increased tear film osmolarity, which occurs as a result of excessive water evaporation with normal lacrimal secretory function. 12 The result of these processes is a hyperosmotic and desiccating environment that stimulates innate inflammatory events

claims.claim: The leading cause of evaporative dry eye is meibomian gland dysfunction, and distinguishing between the categories can be difficult due to overlap of mechanisms, as in Sjogren's syndrome where the effect on the meibomian gland can lead to evaporative dry eye as well
claims.source_text: The leading cause of EDE is meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD), 9 … While the categories of DED exist, often distinguishing between them can be difficult due to an overlap of the mechanisms involved (eg in Sjögren's syndrome). While it is recognised as ADDE, the effect on the meibomian gland can lead to EDE as well.

claims.claim: Posterior blepharitis is often referred to as meibomian gland dysfunction and is commonly associated with rosacea, with signs including redness of the eyelid margin with blocked meibomian glands and frothy discharge along the eyelid margins
claims.source_text: Posterior blepharitis is often referred to as MGD that is commonly associated with rosacea. 14 Signs include redness of eyelid margin with blocked meibomian glands and a frothy discharge along the eyelid margins.

claims.claim: Symptoms of dry eye disease include dry and gritty sensation, foreign body sensation, soreness, stinging or burning, photophobia, intermittent blurry vision, excessive tearing due to reflex tear from corneal irritation, eye fatigue and fluctuating diurnal vision, and symptoms tend to be worse on waking
claims.source_text: - Dry and gritty sensation - Foreign body sensation - Soreness in the eye - Stinging or burning - Photophobia - Intermittent blurry vision - Excessive tearing (due to reflex tear from corneal irritation) - Eye fatigue - Fluctuating diurnal vision … Symptoms tend to be worse on waking

claims.claim: Itching should prompt consideration of allergic conjunctivitis
claims.source_text: - Itching (consider allergic conjunctivitis)

claims.claim: A positive result for the five-item dry-eye questionnaire is a score of 6 or more
claims.source_text: A positive result for DEQ-5 is a score of ≥6.

claims.claim: The ocular surface disease index is a 12-item questionnaire assessed on a scale of 0 to 100 with higher scores representing greater disability, where 13 to 22 represents mild, 23 to 32 moderate and 33 or more severe dry eye disease
claims.source_text: The OSDI is a 12-item questionnaire used to assess the symptoms of ocular irritation in DED and how they affect functioning related to vision. … The OSDI is assessed on a scale of 0-100, with higher scores representing greater disability: 13-22 represents mild DED, 23-32 represents moderate DED, and ≥33 represents severe DED.

claims.claim: Past medical history should cover corneal refractive surgery, contact lens wear and ocular surface diseases, and facial surgery such as in skin cancer management can cause trigeminal or facial nerve damage resulting in neurotrophic keratitis and corneal exposure keratopathy, both of which increase the severity of dry eye disease
claims.source_text: Ask about corneal refractive surgery, contact lens wear and ocular surface diseases such as allergic conjunctivitis, varicella zoster, herpes infections and previous transplants … Facial surgery (eg in skin cancer management) can cause trigeminal nerve or facial nerve damage, which can result in neurotrophic keratitis and corneal exposure keratopathy, respectively - both of which increase the severity of DED.

claims.claim: External examination should focus on skin, eyelids, adnexa, proptosis and visible cranial nerve deficits, mainly the 3rd, 5th and 7th nerves which may affect lid closure and blink rate, and check for eyelid deformity such as ectropion or entropion as well as incomplete closure and infrequent blinking
claims.source_text: The first step is to perform an external examination with a focus on skin, eyelids, adnexa, proptosis and any visible cranial nerve deficits (mainly looking for 3rd, 5th and 7th nerve deficits, which may affect lid closure and blink rate). Check for any eyelid deformity such as ectropion/entropion as well as incomplete closure and infrequent blinking.

claims.claim: Meibomian gland discharge should be a transparent liquid oil, while thick or discoloured meibum indicates dysfunction, and expression of the gland with gentle pressure from a cotton bud can determine whether meibomian gland dysfunction is playing a role and is also a validated way of unblocking the glands
claims.source_text: The discharge should be a transparent liquid oil, while thick or discoloured meibum indicates dysfunction. 5 Expression of the meibomian gland with gentle pressure to the lid margin from a cotton bud can determine whether the leading cause of EDE - MGD - is playing a role. 1 It is also a validated way of unblocking the glands if this is an issue.

claims.claim: Checking visual acuity is an integral part of the examination as worse visual acuity drives vision-related symptoms in dry eye
claims.source_text: Checking visual acuity is an integral part of the examination, as worse visual acuity drives vision-related symptoms in dry eye.

claims.claim: If slit-lamp biomicroscopy is not available an ophthalmoscope with a high plus lens will give better resolution than the ophthalmoscope alone
claims.source_text: If a slit-lamp biomicroscopy is not available, then an ophthalmoscope with a high plus lens will give a better resolution than the ophthalmoscope alone.

claims.claim: The normal tear film height is 0.3 mm and a low tear film height of less than 0.2 mm suggests aqueous deficient dry eye
claims.source_text: The normal tear film height is 0.3 mm (Figure 3B); while this is being assessed, the viscosity and presence of debris and mucous strands should be noted. A low tear film height of <0.2 mm suggests ADDE.

claims.claim: The presence of cells and flare in the anterior chamber is indicative of intraocular inflammation suggesting uveitis, which needs discussion with an ophthalmologist on the day
claims.source_text: The presence of cells and flare in the anterior chamber is indicative of intraocular inflammation, which suggests uveitis, a condition that is linked with systemic autoimmune diseases. 15 This will need discussion with an ophthalmologist on the day.

claims.claim: It is not expected that GPs carry out tear break-up time tests in the office as specific equipment is required, and if these tests are not available referring to a local optometrist is an option
claims.source_text: It is not expected that GPs carry out TBUT tests in the office, as specific equipment is required. … If you do not have access to these tests, then referring to a local optometrist is an option.

claims.claim: For tear break-up time a cut-off of less than 10 seconds is abnormal and relatively specific in screening for dry eyes
claims.source_text: While there is variability in the times of healthy patients, it is agreed that a cut-off of less than 10 seconds is abnormal and relatively specific in screening for dry eyes.

claims.claim: Criteria of abnormality on ocular staining are more than 5 corneal spots, more than 9 conjunctival spots, or lid margin epitheliopathy of 2 mm or more in length and 25% or more in width
claims.source_text: The criteria of abnormality are >5 corneal spots, >9 conjunctival spots, or lid margin epitheliopathy of ≥2 mm length and ≥25% width.

claims.claim: The Schirmer test is performed by placing filter paper over the lower lid margin with eyes closed for five minutes, and although there is no universal cut-off, tear wetting of less than 10 mm in five minutes is considered abnormal
claims.source_text: The Schirmer test is performed by placing a filter paper over the lower lid margin contacting the ocular surface (Figure 3D). The eyes are closed, and after five minutes, the paper is checked to see the amount of wetting. There is no universal cut-off but tear wetting of <10 mm in five minutes is considered abnormal.

claims.claim: Blood tests are usually not required in diagnosing dry eye disease
claims.source_text: Blood tests are usually not required in diagnosing DED;

claims.claim: Patients should learn about the natural history, chronic nature and outcome expectation of dry eye disease, being symptom relief rather than cure
claims.source_text: - learn about the natural history, chronic nature and outcome expectation (ie symptom relief rather than cure)

claims.claim: Advice before pharmacological options includes reducing computer use or lowering computer screen height which reduces lid aperture, increasing frequency of eye rest, avoiding allergens and irritants especially eye drops containing preservatives, humidifying home and work, minimising air conditioners and heaters, and avoiding rubbing the eyes
claims.source_text: - reduce computer use (or lower computer screen height, which reduces lid aperture) - increase frequency of eye rest - avoid allergens and irritants - especially any eye drops that have preservatives - humidify home and work - minimise air conditioners/heaters - avoid rubbing the eyes

claims.claim: Further advice includes ceasing smoking and avoiding second-hand smoke, reducing alcohol consumption, ensuring contact lenses are inserted and used correctly, wearing sunglasses or tinted glasses with wrap-around frames in windy conditions, and increasing omega-3 fatty acids
claims.source_text: - cease smoking and avoid second-hand smoke - reduce alcohol consumption - ensure that contact lenses are inserted and used correctly - wear sunglasses or tinted glasses; wrap-around frames should be used in windy conditions - increase omega-3 fatty acids.

claims.claim: There is evidence that a diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids from fish and plant oils can improve symptoms, with a meta-analysis concluding that the anti-inflammatory effect of omega-3 supplementation on the ocular surface could help dry eye disease
claims.source_text: There is evidence to show that a diet rich in omega-3 fatty acids (from fish and plant oils) can improve symptoms. A meta-analysis concluded that due to the anti-inflammatory effect of omega-3 supplementation on the ocular surface, it could help with DED.

claims.claim: S1 gives the general ocular lubricant dose as one to two drops, or one application, three to four times a day as required, with some patients needing to apply them more frequently
claims.source_text: Generally, the dose is one to two drops, or one application, three to four times a day as required. Some patients may need to apply them more frequently.

claims.claim: Gels provide more extended relief than drops but can blur vision, less so with ointments, and ointments can be used at night if dry eye affects sleep or occurs on waking
claims.source_text: Gels provide more extended relief than drops but can blur vision (less so with ointments). Ointments can be used at night if dry eye affects sleep or occurs on waking.

claims.claim: Preservative-free lubricants are preferred for severe dry eye as preservatives can worsen dry eye disease and cause epithelium toxicity
claims.source_text: Preservative-free lubricants are preferred for severe dry eye as preservatives can worsen DED and cause epithelium toxicity.

claims.claim: Meibomian gland dysfunction can be optimised with lid massage several times a day in the direction of meibomian gland opening, warm compresses applied to closed eyelids for two to five minutes to soften the crusts, and gentle scrubbing of the lashes with eyelid solutions or wipes
claims.source_text: MGD can be optimised with several non-pharmacological methods such as lid massage several times a day, in the direction of meibomian gland opening, warm compresses applied to the eyelids (with eyes closed) for two to five minutes to soften the crusts, and gentle scrubbing of the lashes with eyelid solutions or wipes.

claims.claim: S1 states there is some evidence that applying chloramphenicol 1% ointment topically to the eyelid margin twice daily for one to two weeks can improve cases of anterior blepharitis if eyelid hygiene measures do not suffice, and that doxycycline 100 mg daily for two to four weeks can be used for posterior blepharitis if eyelid hygiene is inadequately controlling symptoms
claims.source_text: There is some evidence to suggest that applying chloramphenicol 1% ointment topically to the eyelid margin twice daily for one to two weeks can improve cases of anterior blepharitis if eyelid hygiene measures do not suffice. 14 Additionally, doxycycline 100 mg daily for two to four weeks can be used for posterior blepharitis if eyelid hygiene is inadequately controlling symptoms.

claims.source_text: Anti-inflammatories such as topical steroids are occasionally prescribed by an ophthalmologist; if used long term, they increase the risk of glaucoma and early cataracts.
